name: Allied Digital Services Ltd
title: Allied Digital Services Ltd - 532875 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Allied Digital Q1 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore, but PAT fell to Rs. 12 crore from Rs. 14 crore on higher tax and margin pressure.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 19% YoY to Rs. 260 crore and PBT rose 19% to about Rs. 17 crore, while EBITDA was Rs. 25 crore at a 10% margin. Trailing 12-month revenue crossed Rs. 1,000 crore (Rs. 1,009 crore). Management said the audit report is now unmodified, with all earlier auditor qualifications resolved. Management acknowledged competitive pricing pressure in the US and India hardware-linked deals, and said margins are under pressure across the industry. Management also said revenue declined quarter-on-quarter, which it attributed to cautious deal-making and delayed large government and hardware-linked orders.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 had net tax benefit of Rs. 0.3 crore
vs Rs. 14 crore in Q1 FY26 (decline)

segments.name: Segments
segments.commentary: The company reports a single consolidated business, with no segment-level revenue or margin split disclosed on the call. Services discussed include managed services, cloud, cybersecurity, digital infrastructure, AI-enabled operations, workspace services, enterprise applications and IT asset management; no per-segment numbers were given.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration of 10x growth over 10 years, about 20% CAGR, with some quarters varying with macroeconomic conditions.
Management expects EBITDA margin of 10-11% currently, and says margins could reach 12-13% once large deals kick in over a couple of quarters.
Management expects new deal announcements from the pipeline in the next one to two quarters (Q2 or Q3 FY27), once hardware prices bottom out and RFPs are issued.
No specific FY28 guidance given; management said timing of margin recovery is uncertain.
capex_capacity: Management says it is investing in AI, people, mid-level leadership and governance, which weighed on margins.
Finance costs rose modestly due to higher working capital deployment as large projects moved into execution.
demand_pricing: Order book: orders of Rs. 120-plus crore booked in the quarter, including new wins and multiyear renewals.

Key wins included a US NYSE-listed electronics company (application maintenance on ServiceNow, Jitterbit and Boomi, entry into US Enterprise Application Services), an Australian mutual bank (workspace services), a Punjab government command and control centre, a Ministry of Commerce body (managed services), an international property consultant (IT asset management) and an Indian FMCG company (IT infrastructure support).
Management said customers are more measured, procurement cycles are longer, and it sees a timing shift rather than weaker underlying demand.
Railway orders of Rs. 180-200 crore were lost after product (hardware) prices rose 25-30% during bidding; the company withdrew to avoid losses.
Competitive pressure in the US market with margin-reduction demands from clients over the last 4-8 quarters; customers seeking discounts in anticipation of automation.
Management said it stayed away from low-margin customer acquisition in Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 due to hardware price volatility, and that revenue declined quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why have EBITDA and PAT margins been declining for 3-4 years, and how can they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited competitive pressure over the last 4-8 quarters, especially in the US, and investments in hiring, leadership and AI. It expects margins to improve in the next few quarters as automation is rolled out to clients.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a threat or benefit, and is it causing revenue deflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called AI an opportunity and a boon. It said revenue pressure comes from two causes: hardware price increases in India and the company's choice to avoid low-margin deals. Exact AI impact will be clear only once automation is implemented at client level.

qa_highlights.question: When will margin pressure bottom out, and what is the FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a timeline because the market is in flux, and that margins are under pressure across the industry as customers seek discounts. It pointed to 10x growth in 10 years (about 20% a year) as the guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What constraints are delaying revenue conversion, and when will growth inflect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said that a hardware price spike of 25-30% led it to exit Rs. 180-200 crore of railway orders. It became cautious on elongated government bids. Pricing from OEMs has now stabilised, and it expects good announcements in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin is currently 10-11%, and it expects 12-13% once large deals kick in over a couple of quarters, with AI investment continuing.

risks_watch: PAT declined YoY to Rs. 12 crore from Rs. 14 crore despite PBT growth, as tax provision rose to about Rs. 4.5 crore.
Other income fell due to the absence of FX revaluation gains after the US subsidiary funding was reclassified from debt to equity.
Quarter-on-quarter revenue decline, which management attributed to delayed large deals.
Margin pressure from US pricing competition and customer discount demands; recovery to 12-13% EBITDA is conditional on large deals and AI deployment.
Hardware price volatility in India affecting bidding on government projects.
Management tone is confident on long-term direction but gave no timeline for margin recovery; delivery on the promised 2-3 quarter order recovery is the key test.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term outlook and the governance clean-up, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and timing of order wins. Management repeatedly framed the slowdown as timing-related and gave no firm date for margin recovery.
key_quotes: We see this as a shift in the timing of decisions rather than underlying demand.
So, the margin trajectory right now, we are anywhere between 10% to 11% EBITDA.
For the first time since the comprehensive review commenced, the audit report carries no qualifications or observations.
So, we are seeing 10x growth in 10 years, which turns out to be about 20% a year is what we are looking at.

growth.why: Long-term aspiration of about 20% a year (10x in 10 years) is not backed by specific capacity; Q1 order book of Rs 120-plus crore and expected deal announcements in Q2/Q3 FY27 give partial support, while management said revenue fell QoQ and margin recovery to 12-13% depends on large deals in a couple of quarters.
